identificationModule.officialTitle: The Turkish Version of the Deglutition Handicap Index

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to test the reliability and validity of the The Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index among adult patients with swallowing disorders.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: The purpose of this study is to test the reliability and validity of the The Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index among adult patients with swallowing disorders.The internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and criterion validity of the instrument will be investigated. The internal consistency will be assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) value with 95 % confidence intervals will be calculated for test-retest reliability. The criterion validity of the scale will be determined by assessing the correlation between The Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index and Turkish Eating Assessment Tool.

armGroups.label: Adult patients with swallowing disorders
armGroups.description: Swallowing function will be evaluated with the Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index, and Turkish version of the Eating Assessment Tool.

interventions.name: Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index
interventions.description: Swallowing function will be evaluated by the Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index.

primaryOutcomes.description: Turkish Deglutition Handicap Index is a swallowing function evaluation tool. The test consists of 30 items which will be scored between 0 to 4. 0 means Never, and 4 means Always. The test score ranges from 30 (minimum) to 120 (maximum) points.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The Turkish version of the Eating Assessment Tool-10
secondaryOutcomes.description: The Turkish version of the Eating Assessment Tool-10 is a self-reporting instrument with 10 questions. Total score ranges between 0 to 40. Higher scores indicate worse swallowing function.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Willing to participate
* Having swallowing problems

Exclusion Criteria:

* Being under the age of 20 years, and above the age of 60 years
* Not willing to participate
* Having no swallowing problems
